cf.title: Fix socket and shared memory handle inheritance on Windows

input.subject: [PATCH] Fix socket handle inheritance on Windows

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducible failure, Thomas Munro agreed with the analysis in message #3, and v2/v3 follow the SOCK_CLOEXEC and socket_set_cloexec() design he suggested. The design copies existing practice: Unix FD_CLOEXEC in pq_init() and the signal pipe duplication in save_backend_variables(). Confidence is medium because nobody has reviewed v2 or v3 and only 3 of 10 messages are visible.

brief.title: Make socket and shared memory handles non-inheritable on Windows
brief.problem: On Windows, programs run by a backend (COPY TO PROGRAM, archive_command) inherit the listen sockets, the client socket and the shared memory handle. If the server dies while such a program runs, the port stays bound and the client connection stays open. A new postmaster then fails with "Address already in use" or "pre-existing shared memory block is still in use" until the program exits.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 adds a backend-only SOCK_CLOEXEC on Windows, which pgwin32_socket() maps to WSA_FLAG_NO_HANDLE_INHERIT, and uses it for listen sockets. It adds socket_set_cloexec() and uses it in pq_init() on all platforms in place of fcntl(). 0002 keeps the postmaster's shared memory handle non-inheritable and duplicates it into each child in save_backend_variables(), as already done for the signal pipe.
user_visible_surface: C API: SOCK_CLOEXEC macro defined for backend code on Windows, accepted by socket creation via pgwin32_socket().
C API: new socket_set_cloexec() function next to socket_set_nonblocking() in src/port.
author_claims: The new tests fail on master and pass with the patches.
Tested with MSVC on Windows 11 across regress, recovery, isolation, postmaster, pg_ctl and libpq suites; v3 passes all CI tasks in the author's fork.
The shared memory fix covers every child process, not only backends.
The v1 test used \copy, so the program was psql's child and the test could not catch the bug.
accept4() support is left out because it only matters for multithreaded backends.
brief.thread_state: Thomas Munro agreed with the analysis and suggested the SOCK_CLOEXEC and socket_set_cloexec() design that v2/v3 follow; Harrison Booth tested v1 on Windows x64 and ARM64 CI. Nobody has reviewed v2 or v3 yet, and the question of Harrison's force_initdb supplement is open.
unclear: Pipe handle inheritance is listed as a problem in message #1 but no patch for it appears.
The material does not say whether the fix is meant for back-patching to supported branches.
The related file handle patch (CF 6197) status and its dependency on this one are not given.
The proposal does not say what happens to handles that extensions or other child-launching code create with inheritance on.
The material does not say how the change affects EXEC_BACKEND builds on non-Windows platforms.
search_queries: pre-existing shared memory block still in use

prior_attempts.title: Close backend file handles on exec
prior_attempts.quote: Oskari, are you planning to answer to this review? As the thread has died 3 weeks ago, I am marking this as returned with feedback.
prior_attempts.reason: The author stopped responding to Peter Eisentraut's review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback about three weeks later. The review asked why EXEC_BACKEND was excluded, asked for an FD_CLOEXEC fallback on systems without O_CLOEXEC, a check of other places that open file descriptors, and a test that lists the descriptors an exec'd program inherits. It also noted that a code comment was wrong because archive_command and COPY to program call execve().
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P18 marked backend files close-on-exec on Unix and excluded EXEC_BACKEND. This proposal covers Windows sockets and the shared memory handle, and it includes a TAP test that runs a server-side program and shows the leak.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: 0001 adds a backend-only SOCK_CLOEXEC macro on Windows and socket_set_cloexec() in src/port; 0002 stops child programs inheriting the shared memory handle.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Programs run by COPY TO PROGRAM and archive_command no longer receive the listen sockets, the client socket or the shared memory handle.

touch_points.reason: New code that creates a socket or a handle on Windows must opt in to SOCK_CLOEXEC or socket_set_cloexec() to keep the fix complete.

questions: Is the fix meant for back-patching, and if so, to which branches?
Message #1 lists pipe handles as affected: will a pipe patch follow in this thread, or is that case no longer a problem?
After 0001 and 0002, which handles in a backend on Windows are still inheritable by a program that COPY TO PROGRAM or archive_command starts?
Does this patch depend on the file handle patch in CF 6197, or can a committer apply the two in either order?
Does replacing fcntl() with socket_set_cloexec() in pq_init() change behaviour in EXEC_BACKEND builds on non-Windows platforms?

committability.owner_note: Thomas Munro agreed with the analysis and suggested the design in message #3, but nobody has reviewed v2 or v3. The owner needs to know the Windows port code and EXEC_BACKEND child startup.
committability.liability: The owner signs for postmaster and child startup on Windows: socket creation in pgwin32_socket() and the shared memory handle passed in save_backend_variables(). A mistake there stops every child process from starting. Back-patching would extend that to all supported branches.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted three versions, reworked the design after message #3, corrected the v1 test that could not catch the bug, and renamed the CommitFest entry on 2026-11-01.

priority.reason: The fix helps Windows servers that run COPY TO PROGRAM or archive_command, and the two patches are small and stay inside Windows port code and child startup. The entry has been in 3 CommitFests and v2/v3 have no review, so it needs a reviewer who can test on Windows.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody could check whether other WSASocket or CreateProcess callers still create inheritable handles, or what access rights the handle duplicated into each child gets. Messages #4 to #10 were not shown.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.summary: Thomas Munro proposed using AF_UNIX sockets for pg_regress and TAP tests on Windows too, removing the Windows-only TCP and SSPI setup code in the test harness. To match Unix security, mkdtemp() on Windows would create the socket directory with access for the current user only.

The author agreed, set the TAP test patch aside for more work and posted only the first two patches. Those later stopped applying, the author posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback.

tested at all on any platform, ie all the TCP-socket code?

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix Windows network event handling
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, the patch moves socket event handles out of each WaitEventSet into a reference-counted per-socket hash table, and adds its own level-triggered event memory, so the edge-triggered FD_CLOSE event is no longer lost. It also changes simplehash for raw malloc/free and no-OOM behaviour, and would let the graceful socket shutdown on Windows be put back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback in the 2024-01 commitfest because CFbot showed test failures and no updated version followed. In review, Robert Haas questioned the simplehash changes: whether SH_RAW_FREE is needed, whether the no-OOM change in 0002 is a good idea at all, and why raw malloc/free is used instead of palloc/pfree. The visible messages show no reply to that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I wonder whether we really want 0002. It seems like a pretty significant behavior change -- now everybody using simplehash has to worry about whether failure cases are possible.

precedents_retrieved.title: socket_timeout in interfaces/libpq
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a socket_timeout connection parameter to libpq so a client stops waiting and disconnects when a non-functional, overloaded server stops responding. The timeout was to be enforced inside pqWait(), the point where libpq clients can wait without end.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier said earlier reviewers did not like an option that forces a cancellation on the connection. He also objected that a timeout in pqWait() skips the cleanup that pqDropConnection() normally does, since pqWait() is written never to time out. Reviewers did not engage further, and David Steele returned the patch, which no longer applied and still had no consensus.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Just with a quick look, assuming that you can bypass all
cleanup operations normally taken by pqDropConnection() through a
hijacking of pqWait() is not fine as this routine explicitely assumes
to *never* have a timeout for its wait.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
Reverted commit(s): Restructure libpq's handling of send failures.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1f39a1c06 implemented write-failure postponement in pqSendSome,
which is above SSL/GSS processing.  However, we've now seen failures
indicating that (some versions of?) OpenSSL have a tendency to report
write failures prematurely too.  Hence, move the primary responsibility
for postponing write failures down to pqsecure_raw_write(), below
SSL/GSS processing.  pqSendSome now sets write_failed only in corner
cases where we'd lost the connection already.

A side-effect of this change is that errors detected in the SSL/GSS
layer itself will be reported immediately (as if they were read
errors) rather than being postponed like write errors.  That's
reverting an effect of 1f39a1c06, and I think it's fine: if there's
not a socket-level error, it's hard to be sure whether an OpenSSL
error ought to be considered a read or write failure anyway.

Another important point is that write-failure postponement is now
effective during connection setup.  OpenSSL's misbehavior of this
sort occurs during SSL_connect(), so that's a change we want.

Per bug #17391 from Nazir Bilal Yavuz.  Possibly this should be
back-patched, but I think it prudent to let it age awhile in HEAD
first.

This feature internally sends SIGTERM to all the backends connected to the

behavior in other cases like pg_terminate_backend(),

fix for this requires further study.

precedents_retrieved.title: In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
Reverted commit(s): Fix corner case for a BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger returning OLD.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Previously, ExecInitModifyTable relied on ExecInitJunkFilter,
and thence ExecCleanTypeFromTL, to build the target descriptor from
the query tlist.  While we just checked (in ExecCheckPlanOutput)
that the tlist produces compatible output, this is not a great
substitute for the relation's actual tuple descriptor that's
available from the relcache.  For one thing, dropped columns will
not be correctly marked attisdropped; it's a bit surprising that
we've gotten away with that this long.  But the real reason for
being concerned with this is that using the table's descriptor means
that the slot will have correct attrmissing data, allowing us to
revert the klugy fix of commit ba9f18abd.  (This commit undoes
that one's changes in trigger.c, but keeps the new test case.)
Thus we can solve the bogus-trigger-tuple problem with fewer cycles
rather than more.

No back-patch, since this doesn't fix any additional bug, and it
seems somewhat more likely to have unforeseen side effects than
ba9f18abd's narrow fix.

roaster_notes.note: The only related precedent, P18, ended because its author stopped replying to review, and the design was never rejected. Its review points (EXEC_BACKEND, a test of inherited handles) are answered here, and file handles belong to the separate patch in CF 6197. The thread names no other earlier attempt.

The proposal adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql command or dump-visible state. Its one contract change, that programs run by the server no longer inherit Windows socket and shared memory handles, matches what Unix builds already do with FD_CLOEXEC. Not checked: whether any extension depends on inheriting the shared memory handle, and whether back-patching is intended. [P18] concerns file descriptors and stopped for lack of a reply, so it does not apply here.

The proposal changes no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL, catalog or wire protocol. The struct changed in save_backend_variables() passes only between a postmaster and children of the same binary. The new SOCK_CLOEXEC macro and socket_set_cloexec() add to the API and break no existing extension API, so neither blocks back-patching.

The patch narrows what programs started by a backend receive, so it removes exposure and adds none; COPY TO PROGRAM and archive_command already need superuser or pg_execute_server_program. The proposal does not say what access rights the handle duplicated into each child gets, and that can only be checked in the code.

No objection from the maintenance angle. The opt-in SOCK_CLOEXEC and socket_set_cloexec() design follows Unix practice and was suggested by Thomas Munro (messages #3 and #5), and 0002 reuses the existing signal-pipe pattern in save_backend_variables(). The changes stay inside Windows port code with no cost on any common path. Two points could not be checked without the code: whether other WSASocket or CreateProcess callers still create inheritable handles, and the pipes listed in message #1, for which no patch is posted. [P18] is a close-on-exec patch for files that was returned after its author stopped responding, not for a design reason.

Postgres has no existing feature, setting or extension that stops Windows child programs from inheriting socket and shared memory handles, and an extension cannot change how the postmaster creates them. The design reuses existing mechanisms: the socket_set_nonblocking() pattern, the duplication of the signal pipe in save_backend_variables(), and the SOCK_CLOEXEC idiom that Unix already uses.

This is a bug fix with a reproducible failure. A Windows server killed while COPY TO PROGRAM or archive_command runs cannot restart until that program exits. Thomas Munro accepted the analysis in message #3, and Harrison Booth reproduced the failure on unpatched Windows x64 and ARM64 CI in message #6. The cost falls only on Windows-specific code paths, so the demand angle finds no objection.
